shape: C, a hybrid of record (OLTP), search and analytics (OLAP), built in stages. Three roles sit behind separate interfaces: the RECORD (entries, immutable revisions, an append-only event log, the lookup log), a SEARCH tier (an exact-handle map plus a fuzzy BM25 index) and an ANALYTICS tier (outcome views). Lineage is served by the record (an edge table plus a recursive CTE). Every non-record tier is a projection that can be rebuilt from the event log. At this scale all three roles live in ONE SQLite file (node:sqlite, FTS5, SQL views). A role moves to its own engine only when a named, measured trigger fires. The plain verdict: a multi-engine hybrid is NOT justified at tens to hundreds of entries [E-04, E-05, E-08, KS-R6]. The smallest hybrid that is justified is SQLite plus a git journal of immutable event files, and it is needed only once a second host writes [KS-R1, X-01]. Meilisearch (search) and DuckDB (analytics) are pre-wired slots with numeric triggers, not components.
name: kb: a staged-hybrid knowledge store (record, derived search and views in one SQLite file; engines split by trigger)
summary: Plain verdict: a multi-engine hybrid is not justified at tens to hundreds of entries. Each extra engine (Meilisearch, DuckDB, a graph store) adds a daemon, a key, an upgrade path or a telemetry switch. None of them adds retrieval or analytics this store needs at this size [E-04, E-05, E-08, KS-R6]. What the shape does contribute is a discipline: the record (entries plus an append-only event log) is kept apart from everything derived from it. The exact-handle map, the symptom search index and the outcome views are projections, rebuilt from the log whenever the canonicalisation recipe changes. All three live in one SQLite file outside every worktree, opened by Node 24's built-in driver, so nothing is installed. The smallest justified hybrid adds one substrate, a git journal of immutable event files, once a second host writes [KS-R1, X-01]. Meilisearch earns a place only if logged lookups show misses that typo tolerance would fix. DuckDB earns one only if an analytic query takes over a second. Every hit must pass an executable gate before anyone acts on it, and the fix text stays hidden until it does. Today I ran control pairs for six of the eight worked examples against git history.

entry_fields.name: entry_id
entry_fields.type: TEXT ULID minted by the writer
entry_fields.why: Stable identity across revisions and hosts with no coordination. The content changes through revisions; the id never does.
entry_fields.prior_art: Immutable identity plus an event stream [T-02.F01]; the KEDB record id [T-05.F15]

entry_fields.name: kind
entry_fields.why: The gate semantics differ by kind. A do_not_apply entry's check is a protective test that must keep passing on a proposed change (R-02 ex6).
entry_fields.prior_art: KS-R9 (do-not-apply entries are first-class); the ITIL known-error type [T-05.F15]

entry_fields.name: status (folded from events)
entry_fields.type: enum wip | not_validated | unverified_seed | validated | known_error_open | conflict | archived | withdrawn | superseded
entry_fields.why: The lifecycle is a fold over events. Entries are retired, never deleted. unverified_seed is never returned as a lead.
entry_fields.prior_art: KCS v6 WIP -> Not Validated -> Validated -> Archived [X-04.F17-F21]; ITIL retire-by-status [T-05.F15]; Smyth & Keane on safe deletion [T-05.F6,F7]

entry_fields.name: title
entry_fields.why: A cheap agent judges relevance from one line. The title states what was seen, not the cause.
entry_fields.prior_art: KEDB symptom-first title [T-05.F15]

entry_fields.name: root_cause_id
entry_fields.why: Two entries can share a cause with different manifestations (ex1 Python TypeError and Node RangeError). The cause is a row, not pairwise edges.
entry_fields.prior_art: Root cause as a row [E-08.f26]; case = problem + solution + outcome [T-05.F3]

entry_fields.name: manifestation_conditions
entry_fields.why: A single root cause is a hindsight artefact. What reuse needs is the cause plus the conditions under which it shows (for example, the start.sh boot-time upgrade under set -e).
entry_fields.prior_art: Cook [T-05.F21]

entry_fields.name: applies_while
entry_fields.type: JSON predicate in entry_rev.body: fix_commits (mainline), dependency ranges, platform
entry_fields.why: Validity is a predicate over code state, never a date.
entry_fields.prior_art: OSV GIT ranges, git merge-base --is-ancestor [T-02.F13-F16]; Linux Fixes: tag, Sentry resolved-in-release [M-03.F24]

entry_fields.name: diagnosis_path
entry_fields.type: JSON ordered steps {observation, hypothesis, check, result, tier}
entry_fields.why: This is the expensive thing to save: the path that found the cause, including where the session escalated.
entry_fields.prior_art: CBR derivation annotations [T-05.F3]; SRE postmortem detection method [T-05.F17]

entry_fields.name: negative_results
entry_fields.why: Approaches that failed, and why, each with a failure-cause class and a scope. Shown as leads, never as prohibitions.
entry_fields.prior_art: ReasoningBank distilled failures [M-02.26; M-01.F24]; RFC 2308/8767 negative caching [T-01.F11,F12,F14]; KS-R2

entry_fields.name: fix_permanent / workaround
entry_fields.why: ex3 has neither yet (it is open), but it has a dangerous naive fix. The two must be separable.
entry_fields.prior_art: ITIL workaround vs permanent fix [T-05.F15]

entry_fields.name: fix_commits
entry_fields.why: PR-branch SHAs vanish under squash merges. I checked today: 9b98c88, c731e66, 8dafcec, 37821f5, a6f9048 and f3dfa6f are not ancestors of origin/main, while their squashes 2fe77f5, da988e2, 6928828 and 1c546a3 are. The write gate refuses non-mainline SHAs.

entry_fields.name: check_id
entry_fields.why: Every lead must pass a discriminating check that reproduces the root cause on current code. A check without a control pair cannot validate an entry.
entry_fields.prior_art: Getafix re-runs the signalling tool [M-03.F01,F02]; X-02 control pair; KS-R9

entry_fields.name: footprint
entry_fields.why: What the entry depends on: files, symbols, config key paths, dependency versions, environment, remote resolvers. Changes to these drive invalidation.
entry_fields.prior_art: Verifying trace [T-01.F01,F02]; X-03 three captures with provenance tiers

entry_fields.name: handles
entry_fields.why: Several fuzzy keys of different granularity per entry, each with a known failure mode.
entry_fields.prior_art: Chromium's three signatures, Crashlytics issue/variant [T-04.F15,F16]; exact-handle tier [E-06.F21]

entry_fields.name: cost_evidence
entry_fields.type: JSON {tiers_used[], model_ids[], tokens_in, tokens_out, wall_minutes, commits, pr} with NULL for unknown
entry_fields.why: Lets the owner see what a reuse saved. R-02 found cost recorded nowhere. Unknown is NULL, never 0.
entry_fields.prior_art: X-05 prospective log fields; C-01 RT-06

entry_fields.name: doc_pointers
entry_fields.type: JSON list of repo-relative anchors (for example docs/HANDOFF-2026-07-28-open-work.md#A2, docs/program/SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md#P12a)
entry_fields.why: The store links to the plan, PRs, git and the register, and never restates them.

entry_fields.name: incident links
entry_fields.why: ex8's second incident had two independent causes. One incident can link to two entries, and one entry can carry several incidents (extend, never sibling).
entry_fields.prior_art: KCS typed many-to-many links [X-04.F17-F21]; ITIL extend-never-sibling [T-05.F15]

entry_fields.name: supersedes / revision_of
entry_fields.why: Corrections are new revisions or superseding entries, never edits in place.
entry_fields.prior_art: PROV wasRevisionOf/wasInvalidatedBy [T-02.F07]

entry_fields.name: version
entry_fields.type: INTEGER, compare-and-set (CAS) on the folded header
entry_fields.why: The few mutable header fields change only by a conditional UPDATE. This is the repository's own try_claim/try_transition idiom.
entry_fields.prior_art: Per-entry optimistic concurrency [T-06.F26; T-02]

entry_fields.name: schema_version / recipe_version
entry_fields.type: INTEGER on revisions, handles and projections
entry_fields.why: Derived keys change when the canonicaliser changes. Raw evidence is kept and keys are re-derived.
entry_fields.prior_art: WER re-bucketing, Socorro's 2,044-signature migration [T-04.F12,F13; M-03.F13,F16]

handle_types.how_built: The scrubbed raw text goes through the recipe-versioned mask pipeline and a tool adapter. The template is prefixed with its context tuple and hashed: sha256(recipe ‖ context ‖ template).
handle_types.how_matched: Exact hash in the exact_handle projection (tier 1); FTS5 porter and trigram substring match (tier 2).
handle_types.failure_mode: Same text, different cause: one alembic CommandError for different targets; a `railway up --ci` timeout that is benign [T-04.F25,F26]. It is never a lead without its context tuple. A recipe change orphans hashes, which is handled by re-deriving from raw.

handle_types.how_built: (tool, phase, normalised command, exit class), for example 'eas build | Run gradlew | eas build -p android --profile <s> | failed'.
handle_types.how_matched: Exact tuple match. Also used as a facet in the prefilter.
handle_types.failure_mode: Too coarse: every Gradle failure shares it. It only narrows and never makes a lead alone.

handle_types.how_built: (method, route template, observed status, expected status), for example 'GET /api/ops/* 500 (expected 401)' or 'POST /api/auth/login 429 (correct PIN)'.
handle_types.failure_mode: Status codes are shared by countless causes. It is weak alone and must co-occur with a template or symbol hit.

handle_types.how_built: The top three in-app frames as module::function, with no line numbers [T-04.F08,F09].
handle_types.how_matched: Exact match on the ordered top-3; frame-set overlap as a fuzzy fallback.
handle_types.failure_mode: A refactor renames functions, so it is recomputed from the stored raw text. A framework-only stack has no in-app frames.

handle_types.how_built: file#json-path with wildcards, for example 'technician-app/eas.json#build.*.env.*' or 'technician-app/app.json#expo.plugins'.
handle_types.how_matched: Exact match, plus prefix match on the file part.
handle_types.failure_mode: A key is moved or renamed. Footprint invalidation flags it.

handle_types.how_built: A repo-relative POSIX path, normalised from Windows forms (C-01 RT-07/09).
handle_types.failure_mode: Over-broad: AppContext.jsx is touched by many entries. A weak type that can reach CANDIDATE only.

handle_types.how_built: A qualified name (logPayment, run_dispatch_once, compare_digest) taken from the fix diff and the check's anchor.
handle_types.how_matched: Exact match and FTS5 token match.
handle_types.failure_mode: Renames and common names. A weak type.

handle_types.how_built: name@resolved-version from the lockfile at the verified SHA (alembic 1.18.5, expo SDK 52, Starlette 0.49.3).
handle_types.how_matched: Exact on name, range test on version.
handle_types.failure_mode: Transitive resolution differs per host, and a remote resolver (the EAS image) is invisible to the lockfile [X-03.F20,F29].

handle_types.how_built: Free-text descriptions by the solver, plus write-time doc2query expansions (other phrasings the solver expects) [E-07.F07].
handle_types.failure_mode: Vocabulary mismatch: my local probe showed 'android build broke' sharing only 'build' with ex7 and ex8. Agents also copy near-matches [M-02.28]. It never makes a lead alone.

handle_types.how_built: The wording of a refuted prescription plus its doc_pointer (ex6: 'gate the lock on the failure path so a correct PIN clears it', HANDOFF A2).
handle_types.how_matched: FTS5 match via `kb lookup --prescription`; exact match on the doc_pointer anchor.
handle_types.failure_mode: The prose doc is reworded or moved and the pointer drifts. The anchor id is used, never a line number.

data_model.history_model: Event sourcing [T-02.F01,F03]. entry_event is append-only, and its ids are sha256 hashes of canonical JSON, so a replayed write is a no-op success (KS-R8; hash chain deferred). Everything else (entry header, revisions index, handles, footprint, projections) is a deterministic fold over events. The bitemporal split is re-anchored [T-02.F09]. Record time is the event's time. Validity is a predicate over git, evaluated lazily at a code state and cached in a validity table that is always recomputable. Corrections are new events: revised, superseded, withdrawn, reaffirmed. Withdrawn entries keep a tombstone, so a replayed old draft cannot resurrect them [T-01]. A near-duplicate of a withdrawn entry is refused unless it explicitly supersedes it. Two revisions with the same prev_rev, which can only happen across hosts, fold to status 'conflict' and both are shown as labelled candidates until a reviewer supersedes them. Mainline SHAs only [T-02.F20].
data_model.provenance_model: Every event carries the following. actor: {model_id, tier, role solver|reviewer|reader, session_id, agent_id}. It is required on every write, because subagent hooks fire with the main session id (C-01). code_state: {sha, on_mainline, dirty:false}. evidence: {kind, artifact_sha256, artifact_path, runner_version, recipe_version}. derived_from: a lookup id or prior event id. The mapping to PROV is wasGeneratedBy=event, wasAssociatedWith=actor, wasDerivedFrom=evidence, wasInvalidatedBy=the footprint item named in an invalidated event, wasRevisionOf=prev_rev [T-02.F07]. Entries are untrusted until their gate passes, because memory poisoning is documented [M-01.F26]. The fold rejects reviewer-only events (reviewed_confirmed, handle_accepted, discriminator_accepted, revised, superseded, withdrawn) whose actor tier is not opus, or whose session equals the recorded author's (X-02: the verifier is never the author). The model id is self-reported, so this is policy and audit, not cryptography (see limits).
data_model.negative_results_model: Two levels. (1) Approach-level: negative_result(entry_rev, approach, why_failed, failure_class wrong_premise | incomplete | worse_side_effect | false_proof | not_reproducible | env_specific, proof executed | argued | reported, scope_digest, evidence_ref). These are distilled and condition-scoped lessons [M-02.26], shown as 'tried in a similar case: X failed because Y', which is a lead and not a prohibition [T-01.F14]. Their life is bounded by the footprint they were observed on: when that footprint changes, they display as 'unverified on current code' (KS-R2). (2) Entry-level: a refuted event scoped to the footprint digest suppresses that entry for that footprint only, and makes it re-eligible as 'needs re-verify' when the footprint changes (KS-R2). The narrowest key is the (entry, footprint_digest) pair [T-01.F11]. The strongest negatives are do_not_apply entries (ex6), whose check is a protective test, so the negative itself is executable. Examples: ex3's 'useState in PaymentModal' is worse_side_effect/argued; ex2's 'target an older revision' is wrong_premise/executed against alembic 1.18.5; ex5's 're-queue is last-write-wins' is wrong_premise/argued with a doc_pointer to the CLAUDE.md known defect, not a copy of it.
data_model.footprint_model: footprint_item(entry, kind, locator, hash, verified_sha, tier). Kinds and hashes: file = git blob OID at verified_sha; symbol = sha256 of the normalised definition block (v1 uses indentation/brace block extraction; later the TypeScript compiler API from technician-app's existing typescript devDependency, and Python ast if the owner rules the interpreter in); config_key = sha256 of the canonical JSON subtree at the key path; dependency = the resolved version from the lockfile; env = probe values (node, npm, python, expo, eas-cli versions; lockfile, Dockerfile and eas.json hashes); remote_resolver = a captured tool-reported line such as the EAS build image or Railpack provider [X-03.F20,F29]. Provenance tiers come from X-03: causal (coverage of the check, phase 2 and needing the owner's coverage dev-dependency decision), declared (the solver's diff and the check's scope paths), cognitive (files read or edited, from the session transcript or hook log; it over-captures) and env_probe. The verifying trace is the set of (item, hash) at the last applies or control verdict, and footprint_digest = sha256(sorted trace) [T-01.F01]. Over-capture only costs a re-verify, while under-capture risks a false positive, so items are pruned only on evidence (X-03). Whole-file OIDs over-invalidate (C-01 warning), which the early-cutoff re-stamp absorbs cheaply for probe checks.

retrieval.canonicalisation: The canonicaliser is code, not a learned miner. It is an ordered, deterministic mask pipeline versioned by recipe_version, with per-tool adapters that prefer structured output: pytest --junitxml, jest/vitest --json, alembic, eas-cli, gradle, railway, HTTP access lines, and Node and Python stack traces [T-04.F01,F05,F10]. Order: (1) scrub (secrets and PII become typed placeholders, X-06). (2) Normalise paths: backslash to '/'; the worktree or repo root to '<repo>'; drive letters and user folders to '<home>' (C-01 RT-07/09). (3) Mask volatile tokens: hex of 7+ chars and SHAs to '<hex>', UUIDs to '<uuid>', timestamps and durations to '<ts>', ports, pids and line:col to '<n>', quoted user values to '<str>'. Discriminating literals are KEPT: HTTP statuses, exception class names, codes such as EAS_BUILD_UNKNOWN_GRADLE_ERROR, alembic subcommands, env-var names such as EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN. (4) Stack traces reduce to the top three in-app module::function frames, never line numbers [T-04.F08,F09]. (5) Every template is prefixed with its context tuple (tool, phase, normalised command), because the same text means different things in different contexts [T-04.F25,F26]. (6) hash = sha256(recipe_version ‖ context ‖ template). The scrubbed raw text is stored beside the template. A recipe change triggers `kb rebuild`, which re-derives every handle and both indexes from raw without touching the record. That is WER/Socorro re-bucketing done as a projection rebuild [T-04.F12,F13,F16; M-03.F13]. Golden fixtures are the eight worked examples' raw symptom strings, plus every new entry's raw text. The pipeline biases toward splitting [T-04].
retrieval.prefilter: Tier 1 is an exact lookup of (type, canonical_hash) in the exact_handle projection, for every handle the query yields: template, tool_phase, http_signature, config_key, file, symbol, dependency [E-06.F21]. Facet filters apply to all tiers. Runtime and tool come from the query's context. For a LEAD the status must be validated or known_error_open; unverified_seed and not_validated may appear only as a labelled CANDIDATE (KS-R9). Entries suppressed for the current footprint digest by a refute are dropped (KS-R2). Withdrawn and archived entries are dropped, and a superseded entry resolves to its successor through v_supersede_closure.
retrieval.ranking: The candidate set has an internal depth of 20 (KS-R4). It is the union of: exact-handle hits; the FTS5 porter BM25 top 20 over search_fts, with column weights templates 5, signatures 4, title 3, symptoms 3, anchors 2, diagnosis 1, ruled_out 1 (proposals); and trigram matches on templates and symptoms for substrings of at least 3 chars [E-01.F04; T-03.F04,F24]. Order: number of distinct discriminating handle types hit (descending), then OOV-aware coverage (descending), then BM25 rank. BM25 values are used as ranks only, never as thresholds, and RRF is never treated as confidence [T-03.F02,F05,F08,F25]. If a second fuzzy engine is ever added (KS8), its list is merged by RRF for ORDER only. The exact-handle tier always stays in the record engine.
retrieval.abstention: The features are score-free and computed by the CLI from the record engine's own vocabulary (search_vocab), so swapping the search engine does not change them [T-03.F26]. (a) Exact hits by handle type. (b) OOV-aware IDF coverage = sum idf(matched query terms) / sum idf(all query terms), where a query term absent from the corpus counts at the maximum idf instead of being dropped. (c) Margin = coverage(top1) - coverage(top2). (d) Validity at HEAD. Why (b) must be OOV-aware: I ran a local node:sqlite FTS5 experiment over the eight examples (not in the register). 'android build broke' matched only 'build', and coverage counted over in-corpus terms came out 1.0 for both ex8 and ex7: a confident false tie. Counting 'android' and 'broke' at max idf drops it below every threshold. The output has three values (Chow's reject option made three-way [T-03.F18]). LEAD requires: at least one exact hit on a discriminating type (template, tool_phase with template, config_key, http_signature with symbol); coverage >= tau_lead; margin >= mu; status validated or known_error_open; validity valid. CANDIDATE requires coverage >= tau_cand and margin >= mu/2, or an exact hit on a weak type (file, symbol, dependency). Anything else is a MISS, which is cheap and safe. A suspect entry is demoted from lead to candidate with the label 'footprint changed since <sha>'. At most one LEAD and one CANDIDATE are shown (KS-R4). The lookup output carries the title, matched handles, ruled-out approach titles and the exact gate command, and never the fix.
retrieval.gate: Every LEAD or CANDIDATE is a hypothesis. `kb verify <id>` runs the entry's discriminating check (see gate_runner) at the current HEAD, or at HEAD plus the agent's patch for do_not_apply entries. It returns applies, not_applies or inconclusive. Only applies unlocks the fix and workaround text. `kb show <id> --section fix` exits 3 unless an applies verdict for this entry at this HEAD is in the event log, because agents copy near-matching records, wrong ones included [M-02.28; T-05.F23]. not_applies is appended as a refute scoped to the footprint digest. inconclusive is recorded and treated as a miss. The check reproduces the root cause, not merely the absence of the symptom, and test-pass alone is a weak gate [M-03.F01,F02,F07]. For do_not_apply entries the lookup shows the warning immediately, because acting on it only pauses a change. The protective check then confirms it against the agent's patch.
retrieval.thresholds: Proposals and owner parameters (KS-R10): tau_lead = 0.6, tau_cand = 0.35, mu = 0.2, internal depth 20. Illustration only, not calibration: in my eight-example probe the right entry had coverage 0.64 to 1.0 with margins 0.37 to 0.75 for paraphrased queries ('manager retried payment and it was charged twice' gave ex3 0.73 vs 0.27). The typo query 'easbuild faild gradel' returned nothing. Calibration happens in KS3 by leave-one-handle-out over the seeded entries plus at least 40 hard-negative and stale probes. The ex7/ex8 pair is the canonical hard negative: same tool, overlapping words, different cause [T-03.F23]. The thresholds chosen are those giving 0 false leads, and recall is then reported. 0 FP in 40 bounds the false-lead rate at 7.5%, and 0 in 60 at 5% (rule of three) [T-03.F19,F20; X-05.F17,F24]. Thresholds are stored in meta with the eval id, and re-calibrated whenever the recipe, the column weights or the search engine changes.
retrieval.feedback: Every outcome is retained (the CBR revise/retain half [T-05.F1]). A not_applies verify appends `refuted` with the footprint digest: the entry is suppressed for that footprint and becomes re-eligible ('needs re-verify') once the footprint changes (KS-R2; a negative is a lead [T-01.F14]). A cheap agent may append two kinds of proposal. `discriminator_proposed` names the query handles that caused the wrong match ('not when X'). `handle_proposed` follows an applies verify on a query whose handles the entry lacked (document-side Rocchio [T-03.F16]). Both become active only after an Opus `kb accept`, or a second independent confirmation from a different session (KS-R3). Helpful and harmful counts are views over events, never mutable counters [M-02.29]. Rejected: pseudo-relevance feedback (drift), LLM rewriting of entries, and LLM-judged contradiction [M-01.F02,F12,F13; M-02.30].
retrieval.measurements: Everything is measured inside the store (KS-R7; the HR skip of a separate pipeline stands). Each lookup row records: scrubbed query, handles, recipe, engine, index_lag, features, result, shown ids, actor model and tier, tokens and wall time (NULL for unknown, never 0, RT-06). Its later outcome is one of applies, not_applies, inconclusive or missed_existing. missed_existing is set when a newly recorded entry's exact handles, or a handle-token Jaccard of at least 0.6, match an earlier MISS. Exact pairwise Jaccard is enough; MinHash is not needed at this size [T-03.F14,F15]. Views: v_lead_precision, v_missed_existing, v_entry_outcomes, stale hits, and reuse by tier (did a Haiku/Sonnet agent finish without escalating after an applies). The pilot follows X-05: Step 0 free recurrence audit (KS0); Step 1 blind replay with raw original symptoms and a grep arm (KS6); Step 2 prospective log with a checkpoint at 20 encounters or 8 weeks and a kill criterion. The engine trigger is measured by `kb eval --replay-misses`. It replays every missed_existing lookup and classifies the cause as typo/morphology (edit distance of 2 or less to an entry term), vocabulary mismatch, or handle gap. Only typo/morphology misses count toward the Meilisearch trigger.
retrieval.embeddings_position: Not now [E-07]. At 200 entries or fewer, lexical BM25 with exact handles is the robust baseline. Dense retrieval fails on identifiers and entities [T-03.F09-F11; E-07.F01,F03]. Write-time handle expansion captures most of the vocabulary-mismatch benefit [E-07.F07]. The trigger is an owner parameter (KS-R10; E-07's inferred ~5% 'missed, entry existed' over 50 lookups, or more than ~1,000 entries), and only misses classified as vocabulary mismatch count toward it. Embeddings would belong to the SEARCH role, never the record: sqlite-vec in the same file (pre-v1, optional [E-01.F13]), or a Meilisearch userProvided embedder if KS8 exists. Vectors would come from a pinned local int8 bge-small via transformers.js with allowRemoteModels=false, with a model and revision stamp on every vector because of embedding drift [E-07.F19,F24,F28]. They would be fused by RRF for order only. Abstention stays on handles and lexical coverage, and the gate is unchanged. Hosted embedding APIs and Ollama are rejected.

invalidation.triggers: Events, never time. (1) A footprint item's hash differs at the target SHA from the stored trace: a file blob OID, a symbol block hash, a config key-path subtree hash. (2) A dependency's resolved version leaves the entry's applies_while range (lockfile at the target SHA) [T-02.F13]. (3) An env probe changes (Node, Expo SDK, eas-cli, Python, alembic). (4) Fix presence changes: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix_sha> <target>` flips. Because the ship plan builds release/drain by cherry-pick only, ancestry is false there even when the fix's content is present, so `git patch-id` is the secondary predicate and the gate is the arbiter (my inference, not in the register). (5) A refuted event on this footprint. (6) A recipe_version or runner_version change. This rebuilds projections and re-runs historical control pairs; it does not invalidate entries by itself.
invalidation.mechanism: A recomputable query, not notifications: LISTEN/NOTIFY-style push is lossy for short-lived CLI agents [E-03.F12]. validity(entry, sha) is computed on demand: for the at most two entries a lookup shows, and as a batch sweep with `kb validity --since <sha>`. The sweep selects entries whose footprint intersects `git diff --name-only <since>..HEAD`, then compares hashes. It is cached in the validity table (entry, code_sha) and can always be recomputed. States: valid (unchanged trace); suspect (an item changed, re-verify not yet run); stale (anchor missing, or check repeatedly inconclusive: the check no longer points at the code); unknown (could not evaluate). Early cutoff [T-01.F02]: a suspect entry's check is re-run at HEAD. Its anchor must still be found, and for a synthetic control the stored mutant is re-applied to HEAD and must flip the verdict. If both hold, a `reaffirmed` event re-stamps the trace with the new hashes (backdating) instead of discarding the entry. A drifted entry is shown only as a labelled candidate (serve-stale inverted [T-01]). Mass invalidation by dirty bits and TTLs are rejected [T-01].
invalidation.who_repairs: Read repair by the reader, restricted to mechanical events [T-01.F18; KS-R3]. Any Haiku or Sonnet agent that hits a suspect entry runs `kb verify` and appends reaffirmed, invalidated or refuted with the runner's artifact hash. The phase-close sweep re-verifies the suspects in batch. Repairs that change content (a new revision of the check because the code moved, a new anchor, a superseding entry) go to an Opus reviewer, never the author of the original, via `kb revise` or `kb supersede`. A stale entry stays out of leads until then. There is no scheduled review sweep: review happens at hit time [X-04].
invalidation.what_cannot_be_detected: The untracked dependencies [T-01.F03]. Remote resolvers that git cannot see: the EAS cloud build image, Railpack's provider detection, and Railway env vars. Captured log lines narrow this but do not close it [X-03.F20,F29]. Production data state: ex2's job_event.kind vocabulary, ex4's dispatch_cursor contents. External API behaviour: Meta WhatsApp, Sentry, Supabase pooler. Callers outside the footprint that start passing different data. Semantic changes that leave the anchor and signal lines intact. Flakiness and non-determinism in test_id checks. Prose documents that drift into contradiction (R-01a found four). Changes in the agents' own behaviour. Cherry-picked fixes make ancestry predicates wrong in both directions; only the gate settles them. Footprints captured without the causal tier (all of v1) can miss a file the cause truly depends on, and under-capture is the false-positive side.

gate_runner.check_kinds: Allow-listed, four kinds [X-02]. (1) structural_probe: `git grep -E` against a COMMIT OBJECT (no checkout, no execution of repo code), scoped to named paths. The pattern must exclude comment lines, and a mandatory ANCHOR pattern proves the probe is looking at the right code. If the anchor is missing the result is inconclusive, never applies or not_applies. Later, ast-grep for comment-aware structure, an install decision [M-03]. (2) library_probe: parameters for runner-owned functions; no stored code. v1 library: json_empty_string_values(file, glob), json_path_matches(file, path, regex), alembic_duplicate_revisions(dir), line_present(file, regex). All read via `git show <sha>:<path>`. (3) test_id: named tests at a pinned SHA, run in Docker. Verdict from junit XML or jest/vitest --json. Supports `--change <patch>` for do_not_apply entries, and transplant mode (test source from passes_at, code from the target). (4) scripted: only with an Opus approval bound to the spec's sha256, by a verifier who is not the author. Example: ex2b's rollback crash-loop needs a scratch Postgres and two code states. Probes run in under 2 s natively, which is why six of the eight examples are gateable before Docker is involved.
gate_runner.isolation: Probes need no isolation beyond read-only git object access. git runs with `-c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=<empty>` so repository config cannot execute anything (my hardening, not in the register). test_id: `git archive <sha>` into a temp dir outside every worktree, applying `--change` explicitly. Dependencies are prepared in a separate trusted step keyed by lockfile hash [X-02]. The container runs with `--network none`, or for backend tests an `--internal` network with a throwaway postgres:16-alpine, because backend/tests/conftest.py TRUNCATEs every table on whatever URL it gets and Settings defaults to localhost:5432 [X-02.F13,F14]. It gets a read-only source mount, tmpfs scratch, an allow-listed env (no FIXFLOW_* secrets, no .env), a redirected HOME, CPU, memory and time caps, and the container-name prefix `kb-gate-`, never the ship plan's fixed Appendix A names. Fail closed: Docker off, image missing or timeout gives inconclusive. Claude Code's own sandbox does nothing on native Windows, and Windows Sandbox has no headless I/O [X-02.F03], so Docker (WSL2 backend now, the same image on the VPS) is the only isolation.
gate_runner.verdict_derivation: The verdict is derived from a runner-owned artifact, never the child's exit code. git bisect run treats 1 to 127 as bad, 127 is command-not-found, Python and Node crashes exit 1, and pytest exits 5 when no tests were collected [X-02.F01,F12]. Probes: the runner writes a JSON artifact {sha, paths, anchor_hits, signal_hits, runner_version} and hashes it. Polarity maps the hits to a verdict. test_id: parse the junit or json report. The named test must be COLLECTED and must fail by an assertion, not an import or collection error, to count as root-cause-present. Skipped, uncollected, errored, crashed or missing reports are inconclusive (the HR skip-aware-gates ruling applies here too). Tri-state: applies, not_applies, inconclusive. 'Could not run' never equals not_applies. Flaky policy: rerun only on disagreement, and applies requires unanimity [X-02]. protective_must_pass: applies (meaning DO NOT APPLY) when any protective test fails with the agent's patch while passing on HEAD.
gate_runner.approval: structural_probe and library_probe need schema validation only, since no code executes. test_id needs the test id to exist at a mainline SHA, so it was reviewed in a merged PR; transplant and mutant patches are stored blobs reviewed at `kb confirm`. scripted needs `approved_by` = an Opus reviewer distinct from the author and `approved_spec_sha` = the spec hash; any edit to the spec voids the approval. Every entry, whatever the kind, becomes validated only through `kb confirm` by an Opus reviewer who re-runs the control pair independently.
gate_runner.control_pair: Required for validation (KS-R9; X-02). There are two kinds. HISTORICAL: fails_at and passes_at are mainline SHAs where the cause is present and absent. SYNTHETIC: a stored fixture or mutant patch that reintroduces the cause on passes_at, used when the hazard never reached main (ex2a) or when the check did not exist before the fix (ex5). The runner rejects a check that gives the same verdict at both ends (no vacuous gate). It re-runs historical pairs whenever runner_version or recipe_version changes, and re-applies synthetic mutants at HEAD during early-cutoff re-stamps. Measured today against this repository: ex1 3 matches at 2fe77f5^ vs 0 at 2fe77f5; ex4 seed INSERT 0 vs 1 and max_event_age 0 vs 5 at da988e2^ vs da988e2; ex7 FAIL at 140428c vs OK at 79a8dd4; ex8 FAIL at 60c026d vs OK at 6928828; Dependabot ignore 0 at 6928828^ vs 1 at 6928828; ex2a 0 duplicate revisions at HEAD. Two naive probes FAILED their pairs. A whole-repo grep for compare_digest matched comments (4 before, 9 after), and a `catch { return; }` grep found 0 at 37821f5 (multi-line form) and 1 at 8dafcec (a comment quoting it). The write gate exists to catch exactly these.

concurrency.write_path: Every write is one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction on the single WAL file (busy_timeout 5000 ms) [T-06.F1; E-01.F10]. Steps: (1) INSERT OR IGNORE the event(s) by content-hash id, so a replayed write is a no-op success (the repository's client_id idiom). (2) Re-fold the touched entry and apply it with `UPDATE entry SET ..., version = version + 1 WHERE id = ? AND version = ?`. Zero rows means re-read and re-fold, never overwrite blindly (the try_claim/try_transition idiom). (3) The projector updates exact_handle, search_doc, search_fts and search_tri, and sets projection_state.last_seq, in the SAME transaction, with explicit statements rather than triggers so it is testable. FTS5 external content needs that discipline or a 'rebuild' [E-05.F24]. (4) COMMIT. The record-to-search lag on a host is therefore 0. Gate runs happen OUTSIDE the transaction, since they take seconds to minutes. Their result is appended afterwards as an event carrying the SHA and footprint digest it ran on, so a slow verify never holds the write lock. Read commands open the file with node:sqlite `readOnly: true`, which the engine enforces (verified today: 'attempt to write a readonly database'). Every runtime that opens the file must have SQLite 3.51.3 or later, for the WAL-reset corruption fix; `kb doctor` and every open assert it [T-06.F4-F6].
concurrency.stampede_control: KS-R5. One `claim` table with a partial unique index on open claims per signature. The signature is the miss's template hash, or the tool_phase tuple when there is no template. After a MISS, the agent about to escalate runs `kb claim <signature>`, a non-blocking INSERT. If a claim is already open, the CLI prints holder, worktree, age and claim_seq, records a concurrent miss, and the agent proceeds anyway. This is advisory: a dead leader blocks nobody [T-06.F13,F30]. claim_seq is the fencing token, and `kb record --claim <seq>` releases it. A second record for the same signature is caught by the write-time near-duplicate check (exact Jaccard) and routed to 'extend, don't sibling' review instead of racing [T-05.F15]. No lease expiry or renewal policy until the log shows concurrent misses (KS-R5). Claims are host-local and never journaled.
concurrency.worktree_story: The database lives outside every worktree. The default is %LOCALAPPDATA%/fixflow-kb/kb.sqlite, or ~/.local/share/fixflow-kb on Linux, with KB_HOME as the override. Every worktree, subagent and parallel session therefore sees one store with no sync [T-06.F2]. It is never inside a worktree, a Docker bind mount, a network share or a synced folder [T-06.F23]. The default avoids Documents, which may be OneDrive-redirected on this box (unverified). The CLI is versioned in the code repo (tools/kb/), and the DB records min_cli_version. An older CLI from a stale worktree opens read-only and says so. Code state is per worktree. Each verify records that worktree's HEAD SHA and on_mainline (`git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main`). Branch-only observations are kept as events but never re-stamp an entry's mainline trace (no Frankenbuild splicing [T-01.F04]). A dirty working tree makes a verify inconclusive unless `--change` is given, so verdicts reflect committed bytes, not working-tree bytes (C-01 RT-04). Events never live on a code branch, so an abandoned branch cannot lose them [X-01.F22].
concurrency.two_host_story: Ranked per X-01. Stage 0, now: the single SQLite file on the dev box is the store. `kb backup` takes a `VACUUM INTO` snapshot, checks it with integrity_check and copies it one-way to the VPS over SSH once the VPS exists. `kb export-journal` also writes immutable event files, so the journal exists before it is needed (KS-R1, stage 0 allowance). Stage 1, triggered when a second host will write (KS7): the journal becomes authoritative. Each event is a file events/<2 hex>/<sha256>.json (canonical JSON) in a dedicated store repo inside KB_HOME, outside the code repo. It syncs over SSH to a bare repo on the owner's VPS: never GitHub, and no third-party control plane such as Tailscale (Headscale or plain SSH instead) [X-01.F10,F17,F20; E-09.F05,F07]. `kb sync` does: git pull (event files are pure adds, which X-01 tested to merge cleanly) -> ingest unknown ids -> refold the touched entries -> push. Each host's SQLite is a per-host projection, rebuildable with `kb rebuild --from-journal`. The fold is deterministic over the event SET (causal prev pointers, then time, then id), so both hosts converge. Conflicting revisions surface as status 'conflict', never as last-writer-wins [T-06.F26]. Cross-host lag = time between syncs, run at phase start and close. The Linux host must run Node with SQLite 3.51.3 or later, and the distro's sqlite3 CLI is never pointed at the file. Search-engine and analytics projections are never synced; they rebuild per host.

engines.role: RECORD (OLTP): entries, revisions, events, lookups, claims
engines.version_or_status: SQLite 3.53.4 bundled in Node 24.22.1 (FTS5 and JSON compiled in; checked today). node:sqlite is Stability 1.2, release candidate. Runtime gate: SQLite 3.51.3 or later.
engines.why: Embedded and built in. Serialised writers, non-blocking readers and atomic conditional UPDATEs in one file. A 4-writer WAL test showed no SQLITE_BUSY [E-01.F01,F02,F10; T-06.F1-F6].
engines.ops_cost: One file and one backup command. No service to start, no key, no port.
engines.install_needed: None. better-sqlite3 (npm) is the fallback driver only if node:sqlite's API changes.

engines.role: SEARCH, stage 0-1: exact-handle tier plus fuzzy symptom tier
engines.engine: SQLite FTS5 (porter+unicode61 table, trigram table, fts5vocab) and a WITHOUT ROWID exact_handle table, all projections in the same file
engines.why: BM25 with per-column weights, trigram substring matching for error text, and a vocabulary for IDF coverage. At this size a search server adds only typo tolerance and built-in hybrid vectors [E-04.F22,F25; T-03.F04,F24]. Being in the same transaction as the record gives zero record-to-index lag.
engines.ops_cost: None beyond the record; `kb rebuild` takes seconds at hundreds of rows

engines.role: ANALYTICS (OLAP): outcome, precision and staleness views
engines.engine: SQL views in the record file
engines.why: About 10^3-10^4 rows against practitioner thresholds of 10^7-10^8 for a second analytical engine [E-05.F22,F26 reported/inferred]; KS-R6.

engines.engine: lineage_edge table plus a recursive CTE (no depth in the UNION key), root cause as an FK row
engines.why: All four lineage queries are a join or one CTE. Measured 0.07-95 ms on a dense 300-node/3000-edge worst case [E-08.f16,f19,f26]. Neo4j, Memgraph, Kùzu and the rest are rejected for telemetry, licence or abandonment [E-08.f1-f18; E-02.F11].

engines.engine: git: a local store repo in KB_HOME plus a bare repo on the owner's VPS over SSH
engines.version_or_status: git 2.56 is installed; the VPS comes from the ship plan (P3b)
engines.why: Immutable per-event files merge as pure adds, the index stays a cache, and it is mandated by KS-R1 [E-09.F05,F07; X-01.F20]. Dolt is the heavier upgrade path, with CLI telemetry on by default [X-01.F17].

engines.ops_cost: `kb sync` at phase start and close; one more repo to back up (it is the backup)
engines.install_needed: None on the dev box; Node and git on the VPS as part of its build

engines.engine: Docker Desktop (WSL2) with postgres:16-alpine and a Node image matching the repo
engines.version_or_status: Installed, AutoStart off. postgres:16-alpine is already used locally and in CI [E-03.F21,F22].
engines.why: The only isolation that works headless on native Windows and is identical on the VPS [X-02.F03,F13,F14]
engines.egress: Image pulls are downloads only. Containers run with --network none or --internal.

engines.engine: Meilisearch Community Edition (MIT). Alternatives recorded: Redis 8 Query Engine (AGPLv3) only if Redis already runs on the host; Tantivy rejected (needs a Rust toolchain [E-04.F15]).
engines.version_or_status: Pin at adoption. v1.56.0 was latest on 2026-10-26, on a roughly two-week cadence. Choose the community asset explicitly, not 'enterprise' [E-04.F02].
engines.why: The only credible optional search daemon. Built-in typo tolerance (1 typo at 5+ chars, 2 at 9+), local-only hybrid via userProvided embedders, a Windows exe and a ~106 MB image [E-04.F02,F03,F07,F08]. Earns a place only when the typo/morphology miss trigger fires. Redis 8 has BM25STD and Levenshtein up to 3 but is RAM-resident with no native Windows build [E-06.F01,F03,F05].
engines.egress: Segment/Amplitude telemetry is on by default. Deployment invariant: `MEILI_NO_ANALYTICS=true` and `--no-analytics`, proven by an egress-blocked smoke test. Embedders are restricted to userProvided; openAi and rest are disqualified [E-04.F01,F07]. Its experimental /mcp route is not exposed, because it would bypass the gate [E-04.F06].
engines.ops_cost: A resident daemon, a master key, asynchronous writes (a task queue; not searchable until the task succeeds [E-04.F05]), dumps across upgrades, ~353 MB exe (reported) or a container, and 256 MB minimum RAM [E-04.F03,F04]. Never backed up: rebuilt from the record. The FTS5 tier stays as the fallback whenever its lastAppliedSeq lags.
engines.install_needed: Yes, an owner decision; run on the always-on host, not the dev box

engines.engine: DuckDB 2.0.x LTS (CLI or @duckdb/node-api 2.0.0-r.1) reading a VACUUM INTO snapshot, never the live file
engines.version_or_status: 2.0.0 LTS announced 2026-10-21; wait for the first patch release [E-02.F01,F06]
engines.why: Only if an analytic view takes over a second or the owner wants joins with external exports (CI history, git log). Reading a snapshot sidesteps the unverified SQLite-scanner READ_ONLY attach (KS-R6) and DuckDB's single-writer rule [E-02.F05,F07; E-05.F17,F18].
engines.egress: Extension autoinstall and autoload must be off, with extensions pre-placed; allow_community_extensions=false, lock_configuration=true [E-05.F19; E-02.F09]
engines.ops_cost: A second SQL dialect for views; lag = snapshot age, printed on every result

engines.engine: secretlint (MIT library) and gitleaks (MIT binary, stdin, fail closed)
engines.why: Built-in regexes plus exact-value redaction cover the known token shapes. These add measured recall (gitleaks 86-88% at 46% precision) [X-06.c]. trufflehog is rejected (AGPL, live verification by default).
engines.install_needed: Yes, an owner decision; v1 runs without them

interface_ops: RecordStore.append(events[]) -> per event inserted | duplicate (idempotent by content-hash id)
RecordStore.casHeader(entryId, expectedVersion, patch) -> ok | conflict; RecordStore.fold(entryId)
ExactHandleIndex.put(type, canonicalHash, entryId); ExactHandleIndex.get(type, canonicalHash) -> entryIds
SearchIndex.apply(docs[], uptoSeq, recipeVersion) -> ticket; SearchIndex.awaitVisible(ticket, timeoutMs) -> bool
SearchIndex.query(canonicalQuery, facets, depth <= 20) -> ranked entryIds only (no engine scores cross the boundary)
Vocabulary.df(term), Vocabulary.N() (always served by the record engine, so abstention is engine-independent)
GateRunner.verify(checkSpec, target: sha | sha+patch | fixture) -> {verdict, anchorFound, artifactSha256, artifactPath, runnerVersion}
Canonicaliser.canonicalise(tool, phase, cmd, rawText) -> {template, hash, tokens, recipeVersion}
Scrubber.scrub(text, mode write | return) -> {text, findings, refuse}
abstraction_layer.swap_story: Search, FTS5 to Meilisearch (KS8): implement SearchIndex over its HTTP API. apply() maps to a documents task; awaitVisible() polls the task until succeeded. Add a projection_state row (engine='meili') and run `kb rebuild --projection search --engine meili`. The record, the exact-handle tier, the vocabulary and therefore the abstention features are untouched. Only the candidate order changes, so thresholds are re-calibrated on the same probe set. The CLI reads Meili only when lastAppliedSeq equals the record's max seq, and otherwise falls back to FTS5, recording engine and lag in the lookup row. Record, SQLite to Postgres (E-03's swap target, if multi-host server-side writers are ever needed instead of the journal): a RecordStore adapter on asyncpg-free node-postgres (an install). SearchIndex becomes tsvector plus pg_trgm, noting that ts_rank has no IDF [T-03.F06], which matters little because coverage comes from Vocabulary. Read-only is enforced by a DB role, not the wrapper [E-03.F14]. Analytics to DuckDB: Analytics.view() runs the same view names over a snapshot file; the views are rewritten in DuckDB SQL. Journal: none to Git (KS7) needs no change to any other interface, because the record is already a fold of content-hashed events.
abstraction_layer.what_leaks: (1) Consistency: FTS5 is updated in the writer's transaction and Meilisearch is asynchronous. awaitVisible() and the lag fallback exist because this leaks, and a caller can observe 'recorded but not yet searchable' in another engine. (2) Ranking semantics: BM25 and Meilisearch's bucket-sort cascade (words, typo, proximity, attribute, exactness [E-04.F08]) produce different candidate sets, so thresholds are per engine. (3) Tokenisation: the trigram minimum of 3 chars, porter stemming, and Meili's typo rules differ, so golden-fixture recall must be re-measured. (4) Atomicity: there is no cross-engine transaction, so the projector is at-least-once and idempotent, and an index can be briefly behind. (5) Dialect: the views use SQLite json_extract and partial indexes, which a DuckDB or Postgres swap rewrites. (6) File semantics: WAL location rules, the SQLite 3.51.3 version gate and SQLITE_BUSY exist only for the SQLite record. (7) Read-only enforcement is an engine property (node:sqlite readOnly, a Postgres role), not an interface property. (8) Gate verdicts depend on Docker and git object access, which no store abstraction hides.

access.how: A zero-dependency Node CLI, `node tools/kb/kb.mjs` (written kb below), using node:sqlite and called through Bash or PowerShell. That is the one path every main session, subagent and workflow agent has with no configuration or approval prompt [E-10.F16]. A skill, .claude/skills/kb/SKILL.md, carries the procedure (lookup -> verify -> show fix -> record), with a description of 1,536 chars or less that is always listed and a body loaded on demand [E-10.F17]. CLAUDE.md gains one pointer line. Nothing is always loaded [M-02 verdict]. Every write needs `--actor <model-id>/<role>/<session-or-agent-id>` or KB_ACTOR; without it the write is refused (C-01: writer identity explicit). The Haiku/Sonnet/Opus split is enforced by command class, not by separate binaries.
cli_commands: kb lookup --tool eas --phase build --cmd 'eas build -p android --profile preview' --stdin < build.log   # MISS | CANDIDATE <id> | LEAD <id>, at most one of each, plus the exact verify command; logs a lookup row
kb lookup --text 'ops endpoint returns 500 when the token has an accented character' --files backend/app/features/ops/deps.py
kb lookup --prescription 'gate the lock on the failure path so a correct PIN clears it' --doc docs/HANDOFF-2026-07-28-open-work.md#A2
kb show <id> --section fix   # exit 3 unless an applies verdict for this entry at the current HEAD is in the log
kb verify <id> [--at HEAD|<sha>] [--change patch.diff]   # applies | not_applies | inconclusive + artifact path; appends the mechanical event
kb record --draft entry.json [--claim <seq>]   # write gate: scrub, schema, mainline SHAs, canonicalise, near-dup, negative-corpus check, control pair -> not_validated | unverified_seed
kb confirm <id>   # reviewer only: Opus actor, not the author; re-runs the control pair -> validated | known_error_open
kb propose handle <id> --from-lookup <lookup-id>  /  kb propose not-when <id> --from-lookup <lookup-id>
kb revise <id> --draft rev.json  /  kb supersede <old> --by <new>  /  kb withdraw <id> --reason '...'   # reviewer only
kb stats precision|outcomes|stale|misses|cost   # at most 50 rows
kb backup [--to <path>]  /  kb export-journal  /  kb sync   # sync only from stage 1
kb doctor   # SQLite version gate, store path not synced/networked, projection lag, CLI vs min_cli_version, telemetry flags of any adopted engine
access.mcp: None in v1. Optional later: a stdio server in the same codebase exposing ONLY kb_lookup and kb_show. It opens the DB with node:sqlite `readOnly: true`, so read-only is enforced by the engine (verified today), because the archived reference Postgres MCP's read-only mode was bypassable in the wrapper [E-03.F14; E-10.F2]. verify, record and every reviewer command stay CLI-only. A .mcp.json server needs an approval prompt in interactive sessions; subagents inherit MCP tools; tool search defers schemas [E-10.F16,F17]. If KS8 lands, Meilisearch's experimental /mcp is never exposed, because it would hand agents raw hits that skip abstention, the gate and the fix-withholding rule [E-04.F06].
access.output_bounding: lookup output is 4,000 chars or less: a lead and a candidate of at most 1,500 chars each, plus the gate command. show is 8,000 chars or less per section unless --max-chars says otherwise. stats is 50 rows or less. --json emits fixed fields. No agent-facing command dumps the corpus; export-journal writes files and prints counts. These sit well under the Bash 30k-char read-back and the MCP 10k-token warning and 25k cap [E-10.F18]. Every returned string passes the return-path scrubber [X-06].
access.read_write_separation: Three classes. READ (lookup's query part, show, stats, validity --dry-run, doctor) opens the DB readOnly, enforced by the engine; lookup then writes its own log row through a separate short write connection. MECHANICAL APPEND (lookup log, verify results, claim and release, propose handle and not-when, record as not_validated): any tier with --actor, events only, never header content (KS-R3). CURATED (confirm, accept, revise, supersede, withdraw, approving a scripted check): Opus reviewer only, and the actor session must differ from the entry's author. The fold also rejects curated events that break this, so a bypassed CLI check still cannot change what lookups return. The limit: identity is self-reported, so this is policy plus an audit trail, not cryptography.

workflow.write_when: Write-through at solving time, never write-back [T-01.F17]. An entry is drafted before the phase closes, and only if the phase fixed a defect or trap AND at least one of these holds: the work needed a tier escalation; two or more approaches failed; it was a build, deploy or migration trap; or a prescription in a prose source was refuted (do_not_apply). The draft is built from what already exists. The ruled-out approaches come from the phase's 'Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections' journal in the PR body. Fix commits are the squash SHA on main. The check is the reviewer's fail-on-base/pass-on-head test or a probe. Trivial fixes are not recorded; swamping is not the threat at this scale, but noise is [T-05.F6,F7]. Retain on failure too: a refuted reuse is recorded on the entry [T-05.F1].
workflow.who_confirms: The phase's Opus reviewer, refuting by default and never the author [X-02; ship plan §0 Routing]. The reviewer re-runs the control pair with `kb verify --at <fails_at>` and `--at <passes_at>` (or the stored mutant), then runs `kb confirm`. An entry without a runnable control pair stays unverified_seed and is never a lead. A second independent confirmation, from a different session that got applies on a fresh lookup, can activate a proposed handle or discriminator (KS-R3) but never validates a new entry.
workflow.read_when: Step zero. (1) Before any tier escalation (Haiku to Sonnet, Sonnet to Opus, or an Opus session starting a from-scratch diagnosis). (2) Before diagnosing a failed build, deploy, migration or test whose cause is not clear after one attempt. (3) Before applying a fix that a prose source prescribes (HANDOFF, G2 register, follow-ups), with `kb lookup --prescription`. (4) When `kb validity` lists a suspect entry in a phase's area. Pull-only: no hook fires lookups automatically in v1. The AGENTS.md finding (>20% cost, no general gain) and the owner's own no-gain record argue against anything always-on [X-05.F12,F21; M-02.32]. A PostToolUseFailure hook stays an owner option after KS6 [M-02.04].
workflow.plan_hook_text: Add to §0, as a new bullet after the 'Resume' bullet: '**Knowledge store (tooling track; never a gate).** Step zero before any tier escalation, and before diagnosing a failed build, deploy, migration or test whose cause is not clear after one attempt: run `node tools/kb/kb.mjs lookup` with the raw error text, the tool and the phase, and put the lookup id in this phase's journal. A `LEAD` or `CANDIDATE` is acted on only after `kb verify <id>` prints `applies` at the current HEAD; `MISS`, `not_applies` and `inconclusive` all mean: carry on as if the store did not exist. Before applying a fix that a prose document prescribes, run `kb lookup --prescription` on its wording; a `do_not_apply` entry that verifies stops the change until the phase's Opus reviewer rules.' Add to the 'Routing' bullet, after the reviewer sentences: 'When a phase fixes a defect or trap that needed a tier escalation, two or more failed approaches, or the refutation of a prescribed fix, the solving agent records it with `kb record --draft` before the phase closes, copying the ruled-out approaches from the phase journal; the phase's Opus reviewer, never the author, runs its control pair and `kb confirm`. At phase close the session runs `kb validity --since <Plan sha>` and names any entry that became suspect or stale in the closing message. workflow.phase_cost: Standing context: the skill's description line (1,536 chars or less) and one CLAUDE.md pointer line; nothing else is always loaded. Per verify: probes under 2 s natively; Jest test_id about 1-3 min; backend test_id with throwaway Postgres about 2-5 min, Docker running (estimates, measured in KS4). Phase close: a `kb validity` sweep under 1 min, plus re-verifies of suspects only. Over the 40 ship phases that is roughly 0-120 lookups and 10-30 entries. workflow.scrubbing: Twice, both local [X-06]: at write (`kb record`, on every free-text field and every handle's raw text) and at every return (lookup and show output). Order: (1) exact-value redaction of the live secret values, read at runtime by NAME from the process env and the repo's .env files; values are never stored. (2) Built-in patterns: postgresql(+asyncpg) URLs with credentials, Authorization and Bearer headers, three-part JWTs, Railway/Supabase/R2/Sentry/Meta token shapes, X-Ops-Proxy-Token values, Pakistani phone numbers (+92 and 03xx forms) and the 5-7-1-digit CNIC form, all replaced by typed placeholders such as <secret:jwt> and <pii:phone>. (3) Optional second pass (owner install decision): secretlint as a library, then gitleaks on stdin, fail closed. (4) A structural rule: raw production-data output (SQL result rows, customer names or addresses, message bodies, drain dumps) is never stored, only templates with typed placeholders, because names and addresses cannot be detected locally. Text tripping a credential-shaped pattern the scrubber cannot classify is REFUSED, not stored redacted. Provider egress cannot be scrubbed away: whatever kb prints enters model context and reaches Anthropic (retention depends on account type; ZDR is Enterprise-only). The return-path scrub is the last line of defence, and the owner rules the scope [X-06.F01-F07; E-10.F31].

backup_story: Stage 0: `kb backup` runs at every phase close and on demand. It takes `VACUUM INTO <KB_HOME>/backups/kb-<UTC>.sqlite` (never a raw copy of a live WAL file [E-01.F11]), runs `PRAGMA integrity_check` on the copy, keeps the last 10, and from P3b on copies the newest to the owner's VPS over SSH, one-way (tested by X-01 under 4 writers: integrity ok, restore then write ok). `kb export-journal` also writes every event as an immutable file into the store repo in KB_HOME, committed locally. That gives two independent recovery paths: the snapshot (fast restore) and the journal (truth, rebuilt by `kb rebuild --from-journal`). Restore: stop writers, replace the file, run `kb doctor` (version gate, integrity, projection hashes). KS1 proves this once: a restore that then accepts a write. Stage 1: the journal is authoritative and pushed to a bare repo on the VPS, never GitHub. Each host's SQLite can be rebuilt from it. Derived engines (Meilisearch, a DuckDB snapshot) are never backed up; they are rebuilt from the record. Nothing lives in the FixFlow code repo, and none of it touches the production backup chain (docs/RUNBOOK-BACKUPS.md is not involved).

limits: The shape's own engines are not justified at this scale. The 'hybrid' is roles and interfaces in one file; Meilisearch and DuckDB are triggered slots, not components, and may never be built.
FTS5 has no edit-distance typo tolerance. A typo query ('easbuild faild gradel') returned nothing in my probe. That is a safe miss, but recall is lost until KS8's trigger fires, if ever.
Vocabulary mismatch ('android build broke') is only partly covered by write-time handle expansion. Embeddings are deferred, so such a query is a miss.
An entry without a runnable discriminating check (ex2b's rollback crash-loop, and many prose seeds) can never be a lead. The store's useful size is bounded by how many problems admit a cheap check.

Text probes are brittle (measured today: comment matches and multi-line forms inverted two naive probes). The control pair and anchors catch this at write time, but probes can still go vacuous after refactors outside their scope; only footprint invalidation and anchors guard that.

Untracked dependencies cannot be detected: remote resolvers (the EAS image, Railpack), production data state, external APIs, callers outside the footprint, cherry-picked fixes (ancestry predicates are wrong on release/drain).
Actor identity and model tier are self-reported. The Opus-only rule for curated events is policy plus an audit trail, not cryptography.
Provider egress is unavoidable. Whatever kb prints reaches the model provider; the return-path scrub reduces this but cannot remove it, and names and addresses cannot be detected locally.
Small evaluation sets: 0 false leads in 40 probes bounds the false-lead rate at 7.5%, not zero; differences between configurations must be large to be believable [T-03.F19,F20].
Docker AutoStart is off, so test_id verifies are inconclusive until the owner starts Docker, and they cannot run while a ship backend phase holds the Docker gates.
node:sqlite is a release candidate (Stability 1.2). A Node upgrade could change its API; the fallback driver needs an npm install.
Two hosts converge by set-union of events and a deterministic fold. Concurrent revisions are flagged for a human or Opus decision, never auto-merged.
There is no measured base rate of recurrence or of cost saved (X-05); ex8 is the only local repeat in the examples. The store may simply not pay for itself, which is why KS0 and KS6 have kill points.
CLI version skew across worktrees is handled by refusal (read-only with an older CLI), not by compatibility.

load_bearing_claims.claim: At up to ~1,000 entries, the exact-handle tier plus FTS5 in the record file returns every entry a dedicated search engine would put in its top 2, except misses caused by typos or morphology, so a separate search engine is not justified until those misses are measured.

load_bearing_claims.rests_on: E-04.F22,F25 (what search servers add); T-03.F09-F11 (BM25 robustness on identifiers); E-07.F01,F03. My local FTS5 run over the eight examples (paraphrased queries found the right entry first; typo query returned nothing) is NOT in the register.

load_bearing_claims.claim: The control pair makes a vacuous gate impossible to validate: any check that gives the same or an inverted verdict at fails_at and passes_at is refused at write time.
load_bearing_claims.falsifiable_by: A validated entry whose check returns applies at a mainline SHA where the root cause is verifiably absent, or not_applies where it is present, in KS3/KS6 stale probes.
load_bearing_claims.rests_on: X-02 (control pair, runner-owned verdict); M-03.F01,F02,F07 (Getafix, SapFix). risks: The store is built and never consulted: it is pull-only and the owner wants less to track. Mitigations: the §0 step-zero sentence, the phase-close validity sweep naming suspects, and the kill points at KS0 and KS6. If it is not used, it is deleted, not maintained.
Engine creep: adding Meilisearch or DuckDB 'because the shape has a slot'. Mitigation: triggers are owner parameters measured only in KS6, and FTS5 remains the fallback forever.

A false positive through a weak check: a probe that matches comments, or goes vacuous after code moves out of its scope. Mitigations: control pairs at write, anchors, absence-polarity probes requiring an anchor, re-verify on footprint change, and fix text withheld until applies.

Poisoned or stale prose seeded as truth: HANDOFF A2 prescribes the fix ex6 refutes. Mitigations: per-entry seeding through the gate (KS-R9), unverified_seed never a lead, and contradictions corrected in the source.

The gate executes repository code at old SHAs (old lockfiles, test side effects such as conftest TRUNCATE). Mitigations: Docker --network none or --internal, a throwaway Postgres, an env allow-list, dependencies prepared separately, fail closed.
Docker contention with the ship plan's fixed-name containers (Appendix A). Mitigations: kb-gate-* names, and KS4 and test_id verifies never run while a ship backend phase holds the gates.

Secrets or customer data leak into the store and then into provider context. Mitigations: scrub at write and at return, refuse unclassifiable credential shapes, never store production output; the residual risk is ruled by the owner.
The store file lands on a synced or network path, or an old sqlite3 binary opens it (WAL-reset corruption before 3.51.3). Mitigations: the LOCALAPPDATA default and `kb doctor` checks on every open.
Squash-merge SHAs: 6 of 13 SHAs cited in the worked examples are off mainline (checked today). Mitigation: the write gate normalises to mainline, otherwise entries cite commits that vanish.
State-owner drift (KS-R7): entries start restating plan or register content and become a second truth. Mitigations: doc_pointers only, a link-only schema for plan state, and open defects not seeded.
node:sqlite API churn on a Node upgrade (release-candidate stability). Mitigation: all access sits behind RecordStore, with better-sqlite3 as an install-gated fallback.

Over-invalidation churn on hot files (AppContext.jsx, outbox.ts) makes test_id entries expensive to keep valid. Mitigations: symbol- and key-path-level hashes where available, early-cutoff re-stamps, and probe checks preferred over test_id where they discriminate.
